classification.difficultyReason: Selects standard circular block, alternating-gap and complement methods for explicitly stated restrictions.

content.prompt: Four boys and four girls are arranged in a circle. In how many ways can this be done:

answer.worked:
Fix one person's position and arrange the other seven people.
$$\begin{aligned}N&=(8-1)!\\&=7!\\&=5040\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: if the boys and the girls alternate,

answer.worked:
Fix one boy's position. Arrange the other three boys in $3!=6$ ways. Arrange the four girls in the four gaps in $4!=24$ ways.
$$\begin{aligned}N&=3!\times4!\\&=6\times24\\&=144\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: if the boys and girls are in distinct groups,

answer.worked:
Treat the four boys as one unit and the four girls as another. Arrange the two units around a circle in $(2-1)!$ ways. Within their units, arrange the boys in $4!$ ways and the girls in $4!$ ways.
$$\begin{aligned}N&=(2-1)!\times4!\times4!\\&=1\times24\times24\\&=576\end{aligned}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: if a particular boy and girl wish to sit next to one another,

answer.worked:
Treat the particular boy and girl as one unit, giving seven units around the circle. The pair has $2!$ internal arrangements.
$$\begin{aligned}N&=(7-1)!\times2!\\&=720\times2\\&=1440\end{aligned}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: if two particular boys do not wish to sit next to one another,

answer.worked:
Subtract arrangements with the two particular boys together from all arrangements. Treating the pair as one unit gives $6!\times2!$ arrangements together.
$$\begin{aligned}N&=7!-6!\times2!\\&=5040-1440\\&=3600\end{aligned}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: if one particular boy wants to sit between two particular girls.

answer.worked:
Treat the girl–boy–girl group as one unit, giving six units around the circle. The two girls can exchange positions in $2!$ ways.
$$\begin{aligned}N&=(6-1)!\times2!\\&=120\times2\\&=240\end{aligned}$$
